clue.text: No peg in oddly shaped hole

indicators.note: something oddly shaped has been bent out of its usual form, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The old saying about a square peg in a round hole: here there is no peg at all, just an odd-shaped gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a gap or aperture, so it is a straightforward synonym for a hole.

clue.text: Use hands to examine friend's head

parts.note: a pal is a friend; the possessive just joins the two parts
pate is an old word for the top of the head

explanation.surface: Feeling a mate's skull to check for a bump.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors palpate a patient by pressing with the fingers to examine the body by touch.

clue.text: Man rising to receive knight with no clothes on

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
receiving something means taking it in, so a letter is placed inside the man's name

parts.note: Dean is a man's first name
K is the abbreviation for knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A chap getting up from bed to welcome a knight while still undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The man's name is the trap: any male name could fit, and only Dean holds a K and turns round correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked describes a person wearing nothing, exactly someone with no clothes on.

clue.text: Kissing cheek's the thing to do — and good!

parts.note: neck means nerve or impudence, as in having the neck to ask
what is in is fashionable, the thing to do
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A peck on the cheek is the fashionable and wholesome greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Necking is informal for kissing and cuddling at length, as courting couples do.

clue.text: Before being bankrupt, company had money to burn

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3 money supply
a business that has gone bust is bankrupt

explanation.surface: A firm that was flush with spare cash shortly before it went under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money to burn' reads as one idiom, but 'burn' is the definition; 'Before being bankrupt' puts the company and money ahead of the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To combust is to catch fire and be consumed by flames, which is what burning means.

clue.text: Zero marks awarded in acting awards

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
scars are marks left on the skin

explanation.surface: A dismal score of nothing handed out at a drama prize-giving.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars are the Academy Awards given annually for film, including the acting prizes.

clue.text: Sulphur Bristol men left out for recycling

indicators.note: recycling breaks material down and remakes it, so the remaining letters are reformed
left out says the letter standing for left is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: the two words supply the letters
L is the abbreviation for left, removed here

explanation.surface: Bristol workers setting sulphur aside to be reprocessed.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one L from the ten letters, then rearrange the nine that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone is the old biblical name for sulphur, as in fire and brimstone.

clue.text: Peace is upheld by man going to church

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the short word runs backwards

parts.note: the word is, turned upwards
Len is a man's name, short for Leonard
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Tranquillity is preserved by a chap heading off to services.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace in the sense of quiet: silence is the absence of noise.

clue.text: Now I'll lie sick, upset with author

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the four words supply all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone taking to bed in distress over a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilkie Collins was a Victorian novelist, author of The Woman in White and The Moonstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie Collins was a nineteenth-century English novelist, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: Anti-aircraft fire coming from RAF Lakenheath

indicators.note: the answer emerges from inside the run of letters that follows, spanning two words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Gunfire aimed at planes from RAF Lakenheath, an air base in Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is the German-derived term for anti-aircraft gunfire, from Fliegerabwehrkanone.

clue.text: Country is home to unfriendly animal

indicators.note: a place that is home to something holds it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: the country in east Asia
a chill manner is cold and unfriendly

explanation.surface: A nation that harbours some hostile creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfriendly' reads as describing the animal, but it is wordplay; the country splits after its fourth letter to take it in.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinchilla is a small South American rodent prized for its soft fur, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Guru entertained by Goering and Hitler

indicators.note: a guest entertained by hosts sits within their company, so the answer lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first name through the middle word into the start of the second name

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher being hosted by two Nazi leaders, an absurdly unlikely meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mahatma Gandhi was often called a guru by followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gandhi was revered as a spiritual teacher and leader, which is what a guru is.

clue.text: Sore knee massaged with paraffin

indicators.note: massaging works and kneads something, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: An aching joint rubbed down with oil as a home remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is the American and technical name for the fuel oil the British call paraffin.

clue.text: Showing ill effects of journey, black stuff used by jewellers protected from cold

parts.note: jet is a black stone polished for jewellery
pipes are lagged when wrapped in insulation against frost

explanation.surface: A long-haul traveller wrapped up warm and laden with black gemstones.
explanation.walkthrough: Lagging is British usage for insulating pipes and tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jet-lagged is tired and disoriented after a long flight across time zones.

clue.text: Ladder under tree growing flaky deposit

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: the lime or linden is a tree
a scale is an old word for a scaling ladder, used to climb walls

explanation.surface: A ladder propped beneath a tree with crusty growth on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Limescale is the chalky crust hard water leaves in kettles and pipes, a flaking deposit.

clue.text: Vehicle moved aimlessly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a light motorcycle with pedals
second meaning: the past tense of mope, to wander listlessly

explanation.surface: A car that drifted about with no clear direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a low-powered motorbike, and the verb's past tense means wandered about dejectedly.

clue.text: Naughty child and scout leader given temporary accommodation

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the preceding word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of scout
a camp is a temporary place to stay, often in tents

explanation.surface: A troublesome youngster and the troop's leader both put up in tents for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, especially a playful child who gets into trouble.

clue.text: Embarrassment ensues when king gets stuck into strong drink after tea

indicators.note: after places the drink section following the tea in the answer

parts.note: cha or char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: something stuck into another thing ends up inside it, so the king's letter goes within the drink

parts.note: gin is a spirit
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch disgraces himself by hitting the spirits after teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance mixed with embarrassment at having failed or been humiliated.

clue.text: With gin, coerce tipsy caretaker

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about unsteadily, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Plying the building's janitor with gin until they are drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge looks after a building and its residents, the job of a caretaker or porter.

clue.text: Discharge of fluid from the nose is punishment for a clergyman on heroin

definitions.text: Discharge of fluid from the nose

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails, a whip once used for flogging
taken as written
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A runny nose is the penalty for a vicar taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is the build-up of mucus in the nose and throat, often streaming out during a cold.

clue.text: One working hard in an orchard?

definitions.text: One working hard in an orchard?

parts.note: surface reading: a diligent labourer, British slang for someone who toils
setter's reading: someone who joins a shoot from one fruit tree onto the rootstock of another

explanation.walkthrough: Graft is British slang for hard work, so the word already means a hard worker; the orchard adds its horticultural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hard worker in British slang and a person who grafts trees together.

clue.text: Fat queen's food store

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The royal pantry belongs to a plump monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard where food is kept, a pantry.

clue.text: Old American with a plan for shopping centre to cover rash development

indicators.note: development turns something into a different form, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece sits around the other

parts.note: a mall is a covered shopping centre
the letters of rash rearranged

explanation.surface: A US planner proposes a shopping centre to hide a sudden outbreak of building.
explanation.walkthrough: George C. Marshall, US Secretary of State, gave his name to the Marshall Plan for rebuilding post-war Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: George Marshall was the American statesman behind the post-war European recovery plan, so he is the old American with a plan.

clue.text: Sailor with beige checked fabric

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor, from tarpaulin
tan is a light brown, close to beige

explanation.surface: A seaman in a beige check pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is a woollen cloth woven in crossing coloured stripes, a check pattern associated with Scottish clans.

clue.text: Kingdom of true majesty

parts.note: real means genuine or true
M is an abbreviation for majesty

explanation.surface: A land ruled by genuine royal grandeur.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the territory ruled over by a monarch.

clue.text: Individual contributing something useful to church or theatre?

definitions.text: Individual contributing something useful to church or theatre?

parts.note: surface reading: a benefactor giving a handy gift to a church or theatre
setter's reading: the gift is the big keyboard instrument found in churches and old cinemas, but the phrase also names someone who gives a body part for transplant

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the instrument donated to a church shares its name with a body part given in transplant surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means a person who gives a kidney or heart for transplant; here it is read literally as someone donating a musical instrument.

clue.text: Insects in "frontless" underwear

indicators.note: without its front means the opening letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: pants are underpants in British usage

explanation.surface: The classic itch of having ants in your pants, with a twist on the garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Ants in your pants is an idiom for restlessness, which makes the surface feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are small social insects, so the plural answer matches the plural definition.

clue.text: Peacekeepers strict about Egypt ignored

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: about means going round, so the second word wraps around the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: a hard line is a strict one
ET is Egypt's code, but E is taken here as its abbreviation

explanation.surface: UN forces taking a tough line over Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that goes unheard is not listened to, which is to say it is ignored.

clue.text: Ring artist with fanciful idea

parts.note: to chime is to ring like a bell
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Phoning a painter who has some daydream to share.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera, after the mythical composite monster, is an illusion or wild fancy that cannot be realised.
